---
title: "Compose the edition"
format: html
execute:
  eval: false
manual:
  page: 13
---

The template provides the order and the section files provide the voice.
Changing the edition should normally mean changing `params.yml` or one of the
section files, not editing the assembled Markdown.

::: {.manual-prereq title="Confirm the prepared material"}

```{bash}
#| eval: false
test -s params.yml
test -s template.qmd
test -s _data/newsletter/events-opportunities.yml
test -s _data/newsletter/articles.yml
test -s _data/newsletter/blogs.yml
test -s _data/newsletter/media.yml
```

:::

::: {.manual-procedure title="Render a candidate edition"}

```{bash}
#| eval: false
quarto render template.qmd --no-cache --metadata-file params.yml --output intermediate.md
```

The result is a candidate publication without the Jekyll front matter that will
be added at the final handoff.

:::

::: {.manual-procedure title="Read the selected sections"}

Open `intermediate.md` and read it as an edition. Check the transitions between
sections, the balance of links and prose, and whether the selected material is
complete for this week's issue.

:::

::: {.manual-check title="The candidate edition is assembled"}

```{bash}
#| eval: false
test -s intermediate.md
! rg -n '\{\{< include|content-visible' intermediate.md
```

:::
